sentences.text: The genus Shaochilong contains only one species, Shaochilong maortuensis.
Based on the length of its maxillary tooth row, the animal was estimated to be 5 to 6 meters long, while a femur length of 61.5 cm suggests a weight of approximately 500 kg.
Its small size for a carcharodontosaurid made it unique among its relatives.
Specimens discovered in Inner Mongolia were first described by Hu in 1964 as a species of Chilantaisaurus before being informally named Alashansaurus by Chure in 2000.
A 2009 re-description by Brusatte and colleagues identified Shaochilong as a carcharodontosaurid, marking the first such dinosaur recognized from Asia.

Fossils were found in the Miaogou Formation at the Maortu locality, though they were originally interpreted as coming from the nearby Ulansuhai Formation, leading to a lectotype establishment in 2010 to address potential multiple individuals.
Due to its small size, Shaochilong likely occupied a unique ecological niche compared to other carcharodontosaurids.
Shaochilong appears more closely related to Gondwanan carcharodontosaurians like Carcharodontosaurus and Giganotosaurus than to Laurasian ones.
The describers of Yuanmouraptor have placed Shaochilong back into the Carcharodontosauridae family.
Shaochilong lived between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago during the Aptian to Albian stages.

Recent research has questioned whether Shaochilong belongs to the carcharodontosaurid family, with some phylogenetic analyses recovering it as a member of Tyrannosauroidea rather than Carcharodontosauridae based on shared autapomorphies found in analyses associated with the description of Tameryraptor.
